content: The test image shows split soybean stems with white/bleached internal tissue and a dark black mass concentrated in the center. This suggests either White_Mold (black sclerotia in bleached stems) or Charcoal_Rot (microsclerotia). Let me check reference images.
I need one more reference from a different class. Checking Sudden Death Syndrome which also shows white pith when split.

**Analysis:**

The test image shows two soybean stems split lengthwise, placed on soil. Key features:
- **Bleached white external stem tissue** — completely pale/white, consistent with late-stage stem bleaching
- **Large dark black mass inside the stem** — this is the critical feature: concentrated black material (sclerotia) visible in the pith cavity
- **White internal pith** — the cream/white pith rules out Brown Stem Rot (brown pith) and supports White_Mold

**Reference comparison:**
- White_Mold (stem/56): shows bleached white stem with dark sclerotia at a node — matches closely
- Charcoal_Rot (stem/108): gray bleached stem but shows tiny scattered microsclerotia, not a concentrated black mass
- SDS leaf: foliar interveinal chlorosis — clearly not this

The concentrated black sclerotia mass inside a bleached white split stem is the hallmark diagnostic feature of White Mold (Sclerotinia). The description confirms: "hard, black sclerotia resembling rodent droppings on or inside stems" and "infected stems become bleached white."
